newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Kim Young-sam associate admits taking Hanbo cash.
newsitem.headline: Kim Young-sam associate admits taking Hanbo cash.

text.p: A close associate of South Korean President Kim Young-sam on Saturday admitted taking money from the founder of the stricken Hanbo Group.
But Hong In-gil, the most senior of Kim's aides to be implicated in a bribery scandal over $5.8 billion paid in loans to Hanbo Steel, denied he made payments to one of Kim's son.
"I accepted one billion won ($1.1 million)," Hong said in testimony broadcast live from a jail where he and others among 10 people standing trial over the scandal are being detained.

The testimony was part of a parliamentary inquiry being conducted in tandem with the trial. A separate probe by state prosecutors has widened the net to include dozens of ruling party and opposition politicians.
Hong has been close to Kim since Kim's days as an opposition leader and is currently a lawmaker who holds a high position in a faction of Kim loyalists within the ruling New Korea Party.
"I have never given money to Mr Kim Hyun-chul," Hong said in reply to a question by a member of the opposition National Congress for New Politics, referring to Kim's second son.
Lawmakers produced little original evidence of wrongdoing by Hong, basing their questions on media articles.

The parliamentary inquiry, which earlier this week heard evidence from Hanbo founder Chung Tae-soo and top bankers, has been roundly criticised in the national media, which has said it was amateurish and ill-prepared.
Hong replied to several questions by saying "I don't know because I don't publish newspapers" or "I don't read newspapers these days".
Before he was detained on February 11, Hong created a stir by saying he was just a "feather" in the scandal -- suggesting he was a scape-goat for more senior figures.
On Saturday, he explained the comment by saying: "To me, there's no distinction between a 'feather' and the 'body'. I was using the word 'feather' as an automatic reaction to a question."
Later, five members of parliament -- four from the New Korea Party and the other from the splinter Democratic Party -- were called in by the prosecution for questioning.
They included Kim Deog-ryong, a member of President Kim's inner circle and one of nine people tipped as the ruling party's candidate in presidential polls later this year.
Upon arriving at the prosecutor's office, Kim Deog-ryong denied taking any money from Chung by saying: "There has never been such an incident."
Earlier on Saturday, two senior opposition lawmakers were released after being questioned by prosecutors based on Chung's testimony that he had given them money.

Kim Sang-hyun of the National Congress has admitted taking 50 million won (US$56,100) from Chung as a "politican fund", but denied it was a bribe. Kim Yong-hwan of the United Liberal Democrats has denied accepting any money.
A prosecution official told Reuters prosecutors discovered that while Chung ordered a payment to Kim Yong-hwan, the money never reached him and was pocketed by one of Chung's aides.
The lawmakers are among the 33 politicians, including 20 current members of parliament, who the prosecution plans to summon for questioning based on Chung's testimony. (Conversion: $1 = 891 won)
